name: DCM Atlantic 1972: Hold the Gap
description:
15 July 1972. Ten days ago, an hour before dawn, the guns opened up along the whole length of the Iron Curtain. By nightfall Soviet tanks were across the Elbe; within the week they stood on the North Sea, with Jutland and the Danish islands behind them. Paratroops came down on Norway's airfields one after another, from the North Cape to Stavanger, and only Oslo still holds. In the south the Black Sea Fleet followed the tanks through Thrace and out past Istanbul, and Cairo and Damascus have thrown open their harbours to the Soviet squadron.

The Navy paid first. The carriers that were at sea when it began are gone, caught in the opening days by missiles from submarines and bombers no one saw coming. Forrestal lived only because she was in the yard: she lies at Norfolk now with her air wing aboard, the last flat-top NATO has in the Atlantic. At Naples the cruiser Little Rock gathers what is left of the Sixth Fleet, and the German, Danish and Norwegian crews who fought their way out wait at Den Helder and Oslo for orders.

Those orders are yours. The Northern Fleet is coming out through the gap between Greenland, Iceland and Britain, with a landing force for Iceland in its wake; another lies in the Sea of Marmara, waiting for its chance at Crete. Soviet submarines are spread across every lane from Norfolk, and without the convoys Britain and the Mediterranean will run out of fuel and weapons within weeks.

Hold the gap. Bring the convoys through. Then take back what was lost: Norway, Denmark, Germany's ports, the Straits, and the Soviet harbours in Egypt and Syria. The war is won when our flag flies over every base beyond the Warsaw Pact's own soil, and lost if theirs flies over everything we hold outside North America and the Western European mainland, Oslo excepted.

texts.guideWar: July 1972. The Soviet Union and the Warsaw Pact struck first: Norway but Oslo, West Germany, Denmark and the Turkish Straits have fallen, and Egypt and Syria have opened their ports to the Soviet fleet. You command NATO at sea: the US Second and Sixth Fleets and the allied navies, from Canada and Norway to Italy, Greece and Turkey.
texts.guideWarTask: Two landing forces are at sea: the Northern Fleet's for Reykjavík (Keflavik falls with it) and the Black Sea Fleet's for Souda Bay in Crete. Stop them, keep the convoys from Norfolk coming, then take back what was lost.
texts.guideHour2: An hour in, the Admiralty orders you to defend Reykjavík and Souda Bay: ACCEPT them (the briefing opens by itself; with a panel open, the badge on the Admiralty icon shows them waiting).
texts.guideHour3: Double-click Naples or Souda Bay: on the base screen, pick a task force and press Sortie.
texts.guideHour4: Select it on the map and right-click the sea where it should go, or use MISSION (bottom bar) to patrol north of Crete.
texts.guideHour6: Press Space or Play (top right). When a landing force is found, the contact screen comes up.
texts.guideExampleMove: The Western Approaches Escort holds south of Ireland. Right-click west of the Hebrides: it plots a route round the coast and shows its arrival time at each waypoint.
texts.guideExampleSplit: Split the frigates off CVBG Forrestal to escort a convoy to the Clyde, then merge them back when it is safely in.
texts.guideLift: Battalions ride in landing ships: Austin 2 · Charleston or Newport 1 (the enemy's Alligators 2).
texts.guideLiftIslands: Select the group and right-click an enemy port: every airfield here falls with its port.
texts.guideExampleInvade: Phibron 4 at Norfolk carries 7 battalions (Nashville and Trenton 2 each; Charleston, Newport and Manitowoc 1 each): enough for a port such as Tromsø, not for a depot such as Alexandria, which needs 15.
texts.guideExampleCarrier: Forrestal loses 6 F-4Js and 2 A-7Es over the Norwegian Sea: back at Norfolk, Replace lost aircraft makes her wing whole, each aircraft she lacks at 15 % of its price. At Faslane (a depot) she can refill her magazine and replace aircraft too; at Rosyth or Den Helder (naval bases, no depot) she can refill her magazine from the base's aviation stores, as far as they go, but not replace aircraft; at Reykjavík, a port, she can't refill it at all.
texts.guideReplen: Sacramento (fuel and weapons), the T2 oiler (fuel) and Kilauea (weapons) are in the Shipyard panel, under Replenishment (their card says what each carries). In a friendly port they load from its stock, never taking it below half of what it should hold.
texts.guideTanker: You have no tanker aircraft in this campaign: the game has no land-based tanker of 1972 (no KC-135 or Victor), and Forrestal's KA-3Bs aren't campaign tankers. How a tanker works:
texts.guideExampleStrike: Forrestal's A-6Es with a Strike loadout on Bodø Air Station from the Norwegian Sea (MISSION: Strike a base, from her AIR OPS) before your landing in Norway: fewer Su-24s to meet your landing ships.
texts.guideDepots: Norfolk, Halifax, Faslane and Naples. They make fuel and weapons every day and send the convoys by themselves; Norfolk and Halifax make most of it, so Britain and the Mediterranean live on the Atlantic convoys. Each makes its own share: lose one, and your side makes that much less.
texts.guideExampleSupply: Souda Bay is about to be fought for: set it to High so its missiles are topped up before the landing comes.
texts.guideExampleIntel: "SOSUS reports surface ships 140 nm from Tórshavn, position approximate": the red circle on the map is that area, not a firm position.
texts.guideCarrierPrices: Their price in the Shipyard panel. Carriers by tier: Forrestal 1,250, Enterprise 1,400.
texts.guideYardsList: Ships join at your shipyards (the crane badge: Norfolk for the US, Faslane for Britain and the northern allies, Halifax for Canada, Naples for the Mediterranean allies), aircraft at the airfield by them.
texts.guideVictory: The first side to hold every base in the theatre but those on the enemy's home soil wins: for you, everything outside the Soviet Union and the Warsaw Pact countries, islands, Egypt and Syria included (Norway, Jutland and the Danish islands, West Germany's ports, the Straits, Alexandria, Tartus...); for the enemy, everything outside North America, the Western European mainland (Oslo excepted) and Greenland.
texts.guideRoad: Stop the landings on Iceland and Crete, get the convoys through, then take back Norway (Tromsø brings Langnes with it), Jutland, West Germany's ports, the Danish islands and Bornholm, the Straits, and last the Soviet squadron's ports in Egypt and Syria (Alexandria is a depot: 15 battalions).
texts.guideFieldModels: (the game's own Keflavik, Akureyri and Reykjavík fields in Iceland, its Reykjavík layout as RAF Gibraltar, Ämari and the Gremikha PVO field for those bases; the game's small US field at Bermuda and Lajes, its very small NATO field at Sumburgh, Vágar, Rønne and Søndrestrøm, the NATO airbase for the other western fields; for the Pact's a Soviet field sized by the base, its East German and Polish versions at theirs, the small fighter field only where no large aircraft are based)
texts.guideReplenStart: Service Squadron 2 at Norfolk, the Sixth Fleet's group at Naples, the RFA tankers at Faslane and HMCS Provider at Halifax start loaded.
texts.guideAllies: (every NATO ship rearms in any allied port; Soviet ships rearm in Pact, Egyptian and Syrian ports and the other way round)
texts.guideBatteries: (NATO: M110 guns; Norway: coastal guns; Soviet: Redut coast-defence missiles and 2S3 guns; East Germany, Poland, Bulgaria, Romania, Egypt and Syria: BM-21 rockets)
texts.guideSams: (NATO: Nike Hercules; Britain: Rapier; Portugal, Canada and France: M42 guns; Iceland: as the US; Soviet: SA-2, SA-3; East Germany, Egypt: SA-3; Poland, Bulgaria, Romania, Syria: SA-2)
texts.guideCaptured: Bases taken in the war's first days start at 55 % of their stocks (two batteries).
texts.guideOpeningWarning: The opening warnings on Reykjavík and Souda Bay come 1 hour in (the Crete landing sails a day in and can be off Souda Bay on the second day, the Iceland landing a day and a half in);
texts.guideEnemy: The enemy plays under the same fog, with its own sensors and reports. Its daily income is 1.5 times what its bases pay (Normal, the one difficulty for now; its bases pay more than yours: 148 a day against 131 at the start). It starts with 182 ships: the Northern Fleet's missile cruisers at sea in the Norwegian Sea, its submarines on the Iceland-Faroes line, south of Iceland, off Halifax and in pairs across the convoy lanes, the Baltic Fleet off Bornholm with the East German and Polish navies in Kiel and Gdynia, the Black Sea Fleet's Moskva and Kynda groups through the Straits, and the 5th Eskadra east of Crete with the Egyptian and Syrian navies. Its East German, Polish and Egyptian squadrons fly from their own fields, the Syrians' from El Nouzha. Its orders arrive in half your time (in half that again while its warships are under half of what it may have, twice your ships), ships at Severomorsk, Kaliningrad and Sevastopol, aircraft at the fields by those yards: first on a front holding under a third of its aircraft, else at each in turn; it can order its newest classes only as the war goes on (more Karas and Charlie Is after about 17 days; Victor IIs, Su-24s and MiG-27s after about 33; a second Alfa only after about 50, and only if the trial boat is lost). It never has more than twice your ships (its own on order counted, landing ships aside), at most 12 aircraft on order at once and never more than twice your aircraft, your carriers' counted, and below 20 escorts it gets escorts back at once, free, as far as twice your ships allow. It organises its fleet into capital groups, surface action groups, ASW and patrol groups and submarine groups; it keeps 4 landing ships on each front, north and south of 47°N (the Norwegian Sea and the Baltic; the Mediterranean and the Black Sea), gathered in a port of that front, and lands with 6 battalions or so, retaking its lost ports first and at once, then going for its objectives (Iceland, the Faroes and Shetland, Oslo, Britain, the Mediterranean islands, Greece and Turkey's coasts), weighing each target's sailing time against the defence it knows there. It raids your groups at sea with 2 to 8 anti-ship aircraft when one of its spotters holds them (a Bear-D or other patrol aircraft, a ship or a submarine), escorted by fighters where they reach; strikes your airfields near its landings' targets and, now and then, the nearest where it knows your aircraft are; escorts its convoys once it loses them on a lane, blockades your ports with submarines, and keeps three fighter patrols of two up. None of its surface ships goes on a mission alone. It doesn't use its replenishment ships.
texts.guideYards: The catalogue's tiers open with your rank (renown {ranks}); a ship's loadouts open by rank too. Ships take 5 to 18 days to arrive (the enemy's half that) and join at a shipyard (Norfolk for American ships, Faslane for Britain, Norway and West Germany, Halifax for Canada, Naples for France; you may pick Norfolk, Naples or Faslane for the American frigates and destroyers; the enemy's Severomorsk, Kaliningrad and Sevastopol); aircraft are delivered to the airfield by a yard: US aircraft by Norfolk (NAS Oceana) unless you pick Naples or Faslane under Join at, the Norwegian F-5s by Faslane (RNAS Lossiemouth, the nearest field), the Canadian Neptunes by Halifax. Only classes in service in July 1972 can be ordered. The enemy's tier grows with the days of war. Prices are the game's own point values (a Gearing 41, a Knox 76, a Belknap 144, a Sturgeon 137, an F-4J 47 each); carriers are priced by tier: Forrestal 1,250, Enterprise 1,400 (the enemy's Moskva 300), and they take longest to arrive: Forrestal 16 days, Enterprise 18 (Moskva 14), every other ship 5 to 15 by its price; replenishment ships: the T2 oiler 120, Kilauea 140, Sacramento 220.
texts.guideVictoryDepth: Each side's objectives are every base but the enemy's home soil (marked in the campaign: the Soviet Union and the Warsaw Pact countries for the enemy, the United States and Canada for you). The first to hold all of its objectives has won; later changes don't undo it. The Western European mainland (the Netherlands, France, Spain, Portugal and mainland Italy, the US bases there included) and Søndrestrøm and Sisimiut in Greenland are not objectives for the enemy, though you must hold them.
texts.guideSamReach: Nike Hercules 70 nm, SA-2 25, SA-3 15, Rapier 4
texts.guideColocated: NAS Capodichino with Naples, Souda AB with Souda Bay, RAF Gibraltar, Çiğli with İzmir, Sinop Airfield with Sinop, Reykjavík Airport, Montijo with Lisbon, Hyères with Toulon, Elefsis with Salamis, RAF Luqa with Valletta, NAS Bermuda with Hamilton, Lajes Field with Praia da Vitória, Akureyri with its harbour, RAF Akrotiri with Limassol, and on the enemy's side Severomorsk-3, Kastrup, Tromsø Langnes, Bodø, Rønne, Yeşilköy, El Nouzha, Babie Doły, Varna and Gremikha with their ports
texts.guideReplenShips: (Sacramento 24,000 t of fuel and 2,150 t of weapons, the T2 oiler 16,000 t of fuel, Kilauea 5,000 t of weapons)
texts.victorySummary: The campaign is won by the first side to hold every base in the theatre but those on the enemy's home soil. Islands count (Iceland, the Danish islands, Crete, Cyprus, Malta...), and each side must keep its own bases too. The Western European mainland (Oslo excepted) and Greenland are not objectives for the enemy.
texts.endingWon: The last base the enemy held beyond its own soil has fallen. The Northern Fleet is back behind the North Cape, the Straits are open again, and the convoys sail to Europe unmolested. The war is won.
texts.endingLost: The enemy holds every base we had beyond North America and the continent. The gap is open, the convoys have stopped, and what is left of the fleet has fallen back to its last harbours. The war is lost.
texts.procurementLift: a place in an assault ship (Austin 2 · Charleston or Newport 1 · the enemy's Alligators 2)
texts.messageVictory: Victory. Every base beyond {enemy}'s home soil is ours: the campaign is won.
texts.messageDefeat: Defeat. {winner} holds every base we had beyond North America and the continent: the campaign is lost.

situation: The Soviet Union and its Warsaw Pact allies opened hostilities without warning ten days ago. Norway from the North Cape to Stavanger, West Germany and Jutland, the Danish islands with Copenhagen and Bornholm, and Thrace with the Turkish Straits have been overrun; in Norway only Oslo holds out. Egypt and Syria have joined them and opened Alexandria and Tartus to the Soviet Mediterranean squadron.

The Atlantic carriers were lost at sea in the first days. Forrestal is the only carrier left, at Norfolk with her air wing aboard. In the Mediterranean the Sixth Fleet has no carrier; Little Rock's cruiser group lies at Naples.

The allies hold what is left: the Royal Navy at Faslane, the Canadians at Halifax, the Norwegians at Oslo, the West German and Danish ships that escaped with the Dutch at Den Helder, the French at Brest and Toulon, the Italians, Greeks and Turks in the Mediterranean.
Everything Britain and the Mediterranean need now comes by sea from Norfolk and Halifax.
enemy: The enemy is on a war footing. The Northern Fleet's missile cruisers are believed at sea in the Norwegian Sea, its submarines across the Iceland-Faroes gap and the convoy lanes from America; Bear-D reconnaissance aircraft are shadowing our groups.

A Northern Fleet landing force is at sea in the Norwegian Sea; Iceland is feared to be its object. A Black Sea Fleet landing force is in the Sea of Marmara with Moskva and Leningrad, and a landing on Crete is feared once it is through the Dardanelles.
The Soviet 5th Eskadra is believed east of Crete with submarines in the Ionian Sea and the Sicilian Narrows. Egyptian and Syrian fast attack craft and fighters operate under its cover.
Further landings are expected against the Faroes, Shetland, Oslo, Britain, the Mediterranean islands, Greece and Turkey's coasts.
intent: Hold the gap. Iceland is not to be given up while there is a ship to fight for it.
Hold Crete. The Sixth Fleet and the Hellenic Navy are to meet the landing before it is off Souda Bay.
Keep the convoys moving. Without the fuel and weapons from Norfolk and Halifax neither Britain nor the Sixth Fleet can fight.
Preserve Forrestal, rebuild the fleet, then take back what was lost.
